notes: Every tunable for T11 Baby Hoover V2. No scoring number, threshold, budget or window may be a literal in the code. Values marked by the papers as REC are provisional; the direction is the finding, the magnitudes are not. Sources: Baby Hoover V2 Offline Decision Layer V1.1, Drama Rev 2 (M-14, value windows, taxonomy), Broadcaster Quality V2, Commentary Channel V1, Driver Naming and Identity V1, Monza reference broadcast analysis.

finish._v9_21: the results programme (SF-07) reads every human from the classification; a correction is now only for a podium place that moved after it was announced

pacing._v9_21: run-away guard (20 OCT spec section 5): the run before a breath is drawn between 2 and 5

lull._v8_1: min_green_s_for: a lull kind may not fire until the race is this many seconds old (the live run of 09 OCT opened on the track temperature).

restart._note: A lobby restart (session end, then session start from suspended) is a new race: retirements, pit/pass bookkeeping, contests and lead history are cleared when the grid reforms. false = V3 behaviour.

restart._about: V9.23: the camera goes to the front when the safety car peels off and again at the green flag

human_finish._about: V8.6: from `laps` to go the camera locks to the human in the closest fight (or best placed); winner, red flag and safety car outrank it

finish_cycle._v9_23: priority 79 -> 82: V9.21 raised booth_focus to 80, which silently beat the finish cycle on 21 OCT (it never ran). Above booth_focus (80) and the pit stop (78), below collision_human (85) and the podium shots (93+).
finish_cycle._about: V9.19 (20 OCT, Dustin): replaces the human_finish lock. Visits the humans in turn: P1-3 14 s, P4-10 10 s, P11+ 6 s; +8 s for a fight with an AI car under 1.0 s (held while under 0.5 s, max 30 s); +12 s for a fight between two humans under 1.5 s, held until a pass (confirmed 2 s, then 4 s more) or a 1.5 s gap, max 60 s. 20 s before a human is revisited, except in a human-vs-human fight. enabled:false puts the old lock back.

podium._about: V9.19 (20 OCT): P1, P2 and P3 each shown onto the line (lead_s before, after_s after; a human longer). Within merge_s of the car ahead it is covered by that shot. enabled:false = winner shot only, as before.

camera._v8_1: 09 OCT live run: 19 cuts in 116 s, every contact in a 15-human lobby pulled the camera for 5 s. Floors raised: normal 4 -> 6, incident 2.5 -> 5, lull 7 -> 10.
camera._v8_22: 14 OCT (Dustin: the camera jumps too much): normal floor 6 -> 8 s, lull floor 10 -> 15 s, max hold 40 -> 60 s, booth_focus minimum hold 8 -> 15 s (its maximum stays the booth's dwell). Incident floor unchanged at 5 s.
camera._v9_21: 20 OCT (Dustin: 20-60 s on good content): normal floor 8 -> 12 s, lull floor 15 -> 20 s, max hold 60 -> 90 s so the battle lock can run; booth_focus 15 -> 30 s at priority 80 (only an Interrupt takes the camera off it); contact takes the camera only when severe (a car stopped or out) or a pile-up (3+ cars, 12 s)

naming._about_full_names: V4 (14 OCT 26): kinds whose {a}/{b}/{c} fill with the roster's spoken.full (intros, grid, podium, results, first contact) instead of spoken.short. Every other kind says the everyday name. A surname shared by two or more cars on track is listed in the blob as never_alone and a model line saying it bare is rejected.

speech._duration_model_about: Pass 3 Part M. A least-squares fit over the 25 Sep render (r2=0.75): about 0.590 s of fixed per-line overhead (onset, breath, decay) plus ~0.246 s per word. Used for the word-budget conversion. VOICE-SPECIFIC: any change of ElevenLabs voice invalidates these constants. per_speaker keeps one shared pair on purpose -- the sample (LEAD 3.13 wps / ANALYST 2.84 wps over 17/18 lines) is too thin to fit two intercepts. apply_to_est_duration is false so the default template run stays byte-identical to the pre-Pass-3 output (acceptance item 1); est_duration_s keeps fallback_wps until a new byte-identity baseline is taken. V8 (09 OCT): refit over run 2 of 08 OCT (76 lines, r2 0.92): overhead about zero (clamped to 0.05), 0.258 s per word; fallback_wps 3.85. Median bias of the old pair on that run was +0.54 s a line.

realtime._about: Pass 4 Parts R-V. The real-time speech channel. Flash is the low-latency model the 226 ms first-byte figure was measured on; eleven_multilingual_v2 is higher quality but does not fit real time and stays for offline re-renders. Voices measured at the same latency floor. character_budget caps one run's spend (account allowance is ~70 races/month, shared); on reaching it the channel stops synthesising but the script and audio kit keep being written. loudness_target_dbfs normalises each clip; trim_silence removes ElevenLabs' leading/trailing silence. voice_settings are iterated in config, never code, and recorded in the manifest. degraded_threshold: once this many synths fail, log that speech is degraded and carry on writing.
realtime._device_about: ENUMERATED on the target machine and used EXACTLY -- never inferred from a name, and NEVER guessed from what a standard VB-CABLE install would be called (that trap: the generic install names the playback endpoint 'CABLE Input (VB-Audio Virtual Cable)', but THIS machine renamed it, so the generic name does not exist here and would fail). The four endpoints enumerated on the machine: 'CABLE In 16 Ch (VB-Audio Virtual Cable)' (16-channel, do NOT use), 'CABLE Output (VB-Audio Virtual Cable)' (the capture side OBS reads, not us), 'Speakers (VB-Audio Virtual Cable)' (THE cable endpoint = device_cable, what OBS captures off the cable -- the authoritative track), and 'ED270 Z (NVIDIA High Definition Audio)' (the operator's real monitor = device_audible). The call is played to BOTH: device_cable (for OBS) and device_audible (so the operator hears it live), in parallel on separate streams. The monitor is best-effort and never disturbs the cable feed; set device_audible to the same string as device_cable, or remove it, to play to the cable only. Both are checked at start-up. --speech-device overrides device_cable; --list-audio-devices prints the exact strings; a real run whose device does not match exactly fails loud at start-up. Re-enumerate and change both strings per machine.

big_moment._about: V9.21 (20 OCT, Dustin: big moments need more passion): the pile-up call, a human taking the lead or a podium place, the big-battle reaction are synthesised with these settings instead of realtime.voice_settings, at most max_per_race a race.

writer._about: Pass 3 Parts L-Q. recent_lines is N in the LineRequest. The word budget is a DURATION budget: slot_budget_s converted to words through speech.duration_model. budget_slack_words is how far a completion may exceed the budget before rejection. sentence_initial_caps_ok is the small allow-list of ordinary capitalised words the checker permits mid-sentence. banned_constructions are substrings a completion may not contain. V8: passage_tokens_per_sentence x sentences (capped at passage_max_tokens) is the completion budget for a passage; passage_max_wait_s is how long the rest of a passage may wait past the previous sentence's end before its tail is dropped. passage_gap_s is the handover gap between the sentences of one passage (instead of the governor's min_gap_s). V8.3 (09 OCT): lead_cloud_s / lead_local_s / lead_passage_s is how long the booth waits for a model answer in flight before airing the template instead; 149 of 170 lines timed out on 09 OCT because the booth aired the instant the channel was free. V8.4 (09 OCT, cycle 2): the window opened -- lead times 3.0/1.0/5.0, cloud max_workers 6, story claims live 16 s so a passage has time to come back; a dropped claim cancels its call.
writer._about_submit_gate: V8.13 (14 OCT): submit_depth is how many claims at the front of the queue (by air priority) hold a model request at any time; the rest wait as free claims and are submitted by the sweep when they reach the front. A must-call (hard, or priority >= submit_must_priority) is submitted the instant it is raised. 0 disables the gate (09 OCT behaviour: 4,070 submissions for 99 lines).
writer._about_tics: V8.16 (14 OCT): stock openers heard as tics on 09 OCT are banned outright; the checker also rejects any line opening with the same two words as a line in the recent window (repeat_opener), names and numbers excepted.

model._about: Pass 3 Part N. Small and fast is the point. max_tokens/temperature/stop go to the Messages API. max_workers threads issue requests on enqueue. The model id is overridden by --model; the key is read from --key-var (default ANTHROPIC_API_KEY) and never written to any artefact.
model._stop_sequences_note: The Messages API rejects a whitespace-only stop sequence (400: 'each stop sequence must contain non-whitespace'), so the old ['\n'] is invalid. 'One line, always' is enforced in code by taking the first line of the completion. Only non-whitespace stop sequences are sent; whitespace-only entries are filtered and the field is omitted if none remain.

local._about: V8 the local lane. An Ollama server on this machine (no key, no internet). Same writer class as the cloud lane, so the checker, cache, stamps and fallback apply unchanged. keep_alive keeps the model resident between lines; the first line after a cold start takes seconds, the rest do not. num_predict = max_tokens. The model name must match 'ollama list'; --local-model overrides it. socket_timeout_s is a transport cap; the air-time deadline still governs when the booth stops waiting.

hybrid._about: Pass 3 Part L, V8 lanes. model_kinds routes those kinds to a model writer; story kinds go to a model writer by default (model_story_kinds); everything else takes the template. V8: the blob's licence.lane picks the writer. fast_lane / slow_lane are cloud | local | template. A lane whose writer is absent (no key, no --local) falls to the other model writer, then the template. V8.6 (09 OCT, league night): fast_lane cloud -- the local model invented colour and gaps; set back to local when a better local model is proven.

blob._about: V6 state blob (State Blob White Paper V1, 08 OCT 26). The slot sets the size: a line inside slow_lane_min_s of its deadline, a hard interrupt, or a sudden incident is the FAST lane and gets notes_fast notes; everything else is the SLOW lane and gets notes_slow (plus notes_lull_bonus in a race lull). spend_* is how many notes the writer is told to use. feel is licensed when the beat's affect intensity reaches feel_min_intensity and a human is its anchor. An interjection is offered for an instant-onset beat at interjection_min_intensity or more, no more than once per interjection_min_gap_s. V8 (09 OCT): sentences_* is the slot's sentence budget on the SLOW lane (the fast lane is always one): the grid/formation and a race lull get the long form, green racing a short exchange, a neutralisation in between. The booth airs a passage one sentence per clip and a higher-priority call cuts in at a sentence boundary.

tether._about: V8 the lead-to-human tether (09 OCT). The start belongs to the leaders and the run to turn one; by halfway the broadcast is on the humans. The human premium in the camera's participation multiplier and in the story scores is scaled by `start` on the first racing lap, rising linearly to 1.0 by lap ceil(laps_frac x total laps). A five-lap race is full by lap three; a thirty-lap race by lap fifteen. enabled=false restores the 07 OCT weighting everywhere.
tether._v9_23: first_racing_lap 2 -> 1: lap numbers are racing laps now (the formation lap is subtracted by the model), in every lobby

start_window._about: V8.3 (09 OCT): from lights out until the leader is frac of the way round his first racing lap (or max_s), the camera stays with the lead group (cuts only inside the top three) and the booth speaks only the lead, the podium, the humans' launch, and a crash as one line; contact and penalties off the front are held and expire. fallback_s applies when the track length is unknown.

dwell._about: V8.3 fix 4 (09 OCT): once a story beat airs the booth stays on that story for dwell_s unless it closes or has nothing queued for idle_release_s; Interrupt rows and the hard race-state kinds break in at once, other must-calls after must_after_s; a story that held the booth for min_for_bridge_s hands the next story a previous_story so the writer can turn from it; a story released less than bridge_window_s ago still hands over
dwell._v8_22: 14 OCT: dwell 25 -> 40 s and idle release 10 -> 15 s for a longer story line; refocus_cooldown_s is the loop guard: a story whose dwell RAN its time cannot open a new dwell (and earns no on-screen bonus) for this long, so booth and camera cannot re-lock on it the moment the next beat lands. 0 disables the guard.
dwell._v9_21: 20 OCT: dwell 40 -> 45 s (half for a story with no human in it), idle release 15 -> 20, must-calls break in after 12 s (a story line lives 16 s, so 20 s let every pass elsewhere expire on the replay) and then as an aside (one per 30 s, camera stays), on-screen bonus 6 -> 12; the battle lock renews the focus by 25 s on every phase change while the pair is inside 2 s, up to 90 s (45 for AI only), and stops renewing after 20 s without a phase or on a stalemate

freshness._about: V8.6: a story line carrying a gap older than after_s is checked against the live gap at air time and dropped (stale_gap) if it has moved by more than the tolerance

start_guard._about: V8.7 (league night 09 OCT): a start-lights event inside stlg_after_lgot_s of lights out is the same start (the game repeats it; it put the booth back into the silent start sequence for whole races); a lights-out event inside lgot_repeat_s is a repeat, not a restart

safety_car._about: V9.23 (21 OCT): the safety car and VSC sequence. The deploy call cuts in (v3.preempt). SC_RETURNING on 'returning' (in this lap), SC_RETURNED on 'returned' (peels off; the camera goes to the front for protected.restart), RESTART kind sc_green on the 'resume race' event inside restart_window_s -- the green flag, called like a start with the leader, P2 and the laps left. quiet_kinds are not said behind the safety car (gap and pace talk about a bunched field). A race that finishes behind the safety car is a finish.

formation._about: V9.23 (21 OCT race test): the game sends LIGHTS OUT when the formation lap is released, with no start lights before it; it was called as the start. A race now starts only on start lights followed by lights out. A lights-out with no lights before it (lgot_without_lights), the formation safety car (SCAR type 3) or session safety-car status 3 opens the formation lap: the lead names it (FORMATION), the analyst explains it (FORMATION_WHY), our drivers' grid is read grid_after_s in (FORMATION_GRID), the field forming up is called inside lineup_m of the line (FORMATION_LINEUP). The lap offset makes the first racing lap lap one. A formation lap that never ends in start lights is taken as under way after max_s with the field at speed. enabled: false restores V9.21 (lights-out always starts the race).

session_gate._about: V8.7: outside a race session the booth is quiet (practice at 21:36 on league night was called as a race's final lap for 21 minutes)
session_gate._about_allow_in_quiet: V9.14 (19 OCT): story kinds that pass the quiet gate in practice and qualifying when a human is in them -- contact, off, crash, first-lap pile-up. AI-only incidents stay silent. The words file phrases them by session (view.session: PRACTICE / QUALI / RACE).

session_colour._about: V8.17 (14 OCT), extended V8.24: colour and the lobby. Outside a race session the booth airs one lore card (hook 'lull') every interval_s, template-written, reading nothing off the race state; UNKNOWN covers the lobby and the gaps between sessions. While Lobby Info is on the wire the lobby segment also airs arrivals, who is still missing and the ready countdown, from that packet alone (never joined to car index: its ordering differs). All of it stops the moment a start-lights or lights-out event declares a race, and never takes the last reserve_for_race 'lull' cards, which the race lulls need. enabled: false turns the colour off; lobby.enabled: false just the lobby lines.

lobby._about_ignore_names: V9.11: lobby accounts that are not drivers (the spectator PC's own game account), left out of arrivals, the waiting list and the ready count.

practice_interview._about: V9.12 (19 OCT): in practice the colour slot alternates one interview line and one lore card. per_driver lines per driver from his Sienna card (facts 2 and 3; reserve_headline keeps fact 1 for the grid intro before the lights), then up to extra more from whoever has spare, least recently featured first. interval_s replaces session_colour.interval_s in practice. The race keeps everything not spent here.
practice_interview._per_lore: V9.22 (21 OCT, Dustin: double the interviews): two interview slots for every lore slot; per_driver 2 -> 4, extra 2 -> 4. The race keeps each driver's headline line and his podium / win / retire lines.
practice_interview._v9_22: V9.22 (21 OCT): kinds: the sessions that air interview lines (practice). mix (off for 21 OCT, Dustin: interviews only need to get in): when enabled, a charity card airs only while charities <= interviews aired this session and a sponsor read only while sponsors < interviews; hold_when_dry keeps them waiting once the interviews run out.

timed_session._about: V8.25 (14 OCT): the practice / qualifying programme (Day Programme white paper 4, 5, 7.6). Calls on cars in the timed sessions: explainer at open, personal bests with stakes, provisional pole, the board as gaps, clock marks, deleted laps, the grid from the classification.
timed_session._v9_23: min_lap_ms / plausible_frac: a lap time under the floor or under this fraction of the session's quickest is a partial lap and is not a time (21 OCT: 'Albon, a zero fifty-seven point two'). A session classified early says its summary / grid at once and nothing after it; a clock that restarts after the classification is not a new session.

v3._about_penalty_reason: V8.20 (14 OCT): every penalty line carries the game's own reason (the PENA event's infringement type, spoken via INFRINGEMENT_WORDS) when no contact story names a cause. Absent from the V3 config so the identity gate holds.

udp._about: V9.11 (19 OCT): one telemetry source. auto = lock to the loopback sender (the spectator game on this PC) the moment it speaks, else the first sender after lock_grace_s; any = feed every packet (the behaviour before 19 OCT); or an IP address to lock to. Other senders are counted in the manifest and ignored. On 09 OCT two local drivers' games were broadcasting onto the LAN and 28% of the packets Hoover modelled were theirs.
udp._v9_21: the game re-sends event packets by design; the duplicate warning speaks only past 2% of the feed

humor._about: V9.15 (19 OCT): lines in the words file or lore cards marked register: humor. Caps per session, spacing between two, never in the start sequence, the final lap or the finish, never within incident_gap_s of a human incident. Every humor line is also marked once (said once a night).

exchange._about: V9.15 (19 OCT): a words-file variant may carry `then` (the other voice's reaction, aired as the next clip). At most one such pair every every_s so pairs do not double the channel load.

_about_v4: V4 config (07 OCT 26): hoover_config_v3.json frozen at Pass 4 for the V3 tool and the identity gate; this file is what the V4 tool reads by default. Same shape as v3 plus v3.restart and the 07 OCT lull/camera values.
